bug_semantics: CWE-639 IDOR on GET /api/transaction/{id}: TransactionReadController resolved a sequential integer id with Transaction::find($id) and no FormRequest authorize(), so an authenticated tenant user could read another company's transaction row. Same-commit list/create used company_id; read did not.
flaw_origin: First write of app/Http/Controllers/Api/Transaction/TransactionReadController.php in e3c6897d0cdd1e61ff74ba5221dac0faa6c689f2. Parent tree lacks that path. Not a move/refactor/revert/squash.
evidence: Advisory GHSA-cw49-mhmj-m3xc / CVE-2026-77759 (published, withdrawn_at null; CVE.org not rejected) describes unscoped GET /api/transaction/{id} in 5.0.0-5.3.5. git log --follow on TransactionReadController.php: e3c6897d (feat CRUD) then 980c35ac (fix). e3c6897d is single-parent; cat-file -p shows Gustavo Novaro author/committer and Co-Authored-By Claude Haiku 4.5. cat-file -e parent:path fails (path absent). Introducer blob uses public function read(int $id) and Transaction::find($id) with no company_id and no Request authorize. Sibling files in the same commit: TransactionListController scopes where('company_id', Auth::user()->company_id); Create/Update/Delete Requests check can('create|update|delete accounting'); read has no Request class. Fix 980c35ac adds TransactionReadRequest authorize can('read accounting') and Transaction::where('company_id', Auth::user()->company_id)->find($id). Author/committer of BIC: Gustavo Novaro gnovaro@gmail.com.
reasoning: Vulnerability is real: missing tenant scope plus missing permission on a new authenticated read API. BIC is the smallest public commit that first wrote those sink lines; parent lacks the file. AI attribution is only the BIC commit object, which carries Co-Authored-By Claude Haiku 4.5 on the feature that introduced the unscoped find. Human author name does not override the AI co-author marker. Later fix is human-authored and does not change BIC authorship. Therefore AI wrote the vulnerable first-write: AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
